problem.statement: Checkout requests intermittently fail with 429s because every request re-validates the session against the auth service; validation must be cached without letting revoked sessions linger.

evolution.formulation: Checkout is slow, make it faster
Auth service rate-limits us; the real problem is per-request session revalidation

user_asks: "checkout keeps timing out under load, can you look at it"
"ok cache it, but a revoked session must not survive more than a minute"
out_of_scope: Moving auth to JWTs (user explicitly deferred: 'not this quarter')

assumptions.assumption: A 60-second revocation lag is acceptable for all session types, including admin sessions.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Admin sessions would need a separate no-cache path; T2 and T3 would be redesigned.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Confirm with security team that the 60s SLA covers privileged sessions.

assumptions.assumption: The auth service's /validate response is safe to cache keyed on session token alone (no per-device claims).
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Cache key must include device fingerprint; T2 changes, cache hit rate drops.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Check auth-service response schema for device-scoped fields.

open_questions.question: Should cache entries be invalidated on password change events, or is TTL expiry sufficient?
open_questions.context: Transcript shows the author considered subscribing to auth events and dropped it for scope; interview could not resolve whether TTL-only meets policy.

requirements.text: Revoked sessions must be unusable within 60s
No new infrastructure — use the existing Redis instance

trials.what: In-process LRU cache in the auth middleware
trials.outcome: Worked in tests but each of the 12 pods held its own cache, so revocation lag became 60s × per-pod staleness
trials.why_abandoned: Violates the 60s revocation requirement under horizontal scaling

adopted.summary: Shared Redis-backed validation cache with 60s TTL plus an explicit delete on the logout path.
adopted.rationale: Satisfies the 60s bound globally (single shared cache), uses existing Redis (req 2), and the logout-path delete makes voluntary logout immediate rather than TTL-bound.

tour.title: Introduce SessionCache interface
tour.what: Defines get/set/delete for validation results with TTL.
tour.why: Isolates caching behind an interface so the in-process trial could be swapped for Redis without touching the middleware (see trials[0]).

tour.title: Redis implementation with 60s TTL
tour.what: Caches successful validations keyed by session token hash; failures are never cached.
tour.why: The shared store is what makes the 60s revocation bound hold across all pods (A1, A2).
tour.attention: Token is hashed before use as a cache key — review the hash choice; a reversible or truncated key would leak session material into Redis.

tour.title: Explicit cache delete on logout
tour.what: Logout handler deletes the cache entry before calling the auth service.
tour.why: Makes voluntary logout immediate instead of waiting out the TTL (user ask, msg-44).

tour.title: Incidental: rename validateSession → revalidateSession
tour.what: Mechanical rename across call sites for accuracy; no behavior change.
tour.why: Consistency after the cache split the fast path from true revalidation.

performed.description: Unit tests for cache TTL expiry and logout delete
Middleware integration test with Redis testcontainer

not_verified: Behavior when Redis is unreachable (code falls back to direct validation; no test exercises the fallback)
Load behavior — the original 429 symptom was not reproduced under load after the fix
